_about._note: Regression thresholds enforced by `python tasks.py bench` and by CI. A metric ending in _min is a floor (must stay above), anything else is a limit (must stay below). Keys starting with _ are documentation and are not compared. Timing limits are set to roughly 3-4x the values measured on the machine recorded in bench/results/*.json, because shared CI runners are slower and noisy: they catch order-of-magnitude regressions, not drift. Correctness floors are exact (100%, 0) because anything else is a defect.

noop_rebuild_1000_rules._note: The spec's target is a no-op rebuild of 1k rules under 500 ms; 311 ms p95 was measured locally. The CI limit is looser so a slow shared runner does not fail the build; the README reports the measured number.

replay_savings._note: The spec's target is >= 80% of LLM calls and tokens saved across the 30-commit replay. Measured: 97.6% median / 92.7% total calls, 91.2% median / 88.8% total tokens.

replay_correctness._note: Not performance: a failure here means the incremental build produced a value a clean rebuild would not, or did work it did not need to.

replay_ablations._note: Each ablation must cost meaningfully more than the full system. Measured over 30 commits: 1.23x rules executed in aggregate without early cutoff (up to 14x on a single commit, where the mechanism actually bites), and 2.65x LLM calls without step memoization.

naive_cache_staleness._note: The baselines must actually go stale, or the comparison proves nothing. Measured over 30 commits: 91 stale artifacts for the input-hash cache, 2 for the prompt-hash cache (the model-id commits).
